title: Correlation is not agreement
statement: Judge whether one measure, such as a model marker, can replace another by how far and which way individual scores differ, not by correlation, which misses a uniformly generous marker.
example: In one simulation, two item banks' scores for the same students correlated at 0.902 yet had 95% limits of agreement of −11.4 to +11.1 points.
detail: A reading assessment's simulation scored the same 2,000 simulated students on its own bank and on a synthetic bank modelled on the reference test's pool, using the standard method-comparison approach: the two scores correlated at 0.902, but the 95% limits of agreement ran from −11.4 to +11.1 points. Its authoritative later run gave 0.918 with limits of −10.0 to +10.0. The package also notes that its ability-recovery correlation of 0.948 measures ranking accuracy, not absolute accuracy.
against: The second bank was synthetic, so this measures the engine's internal consistency, not agreement with the real test: "It is emphatically not a measurement of agreement with NWEA MAP — the comparison bank is synthetic." (`grade3-reading/ti-courseplans/courses/map-proxy-assessment/validity/03_SIMULATION_EVIDENCE.md`, line 220). The narrower band expected after linking is "a hope stated in advance, not a result" (`grade3-reading/ti-courseplans/courses/map-proxy-assessment/validity/04_CONCURRENT_VALIDITY_PLAN.md`, line 25). The generosity is a prediction carried over from research on estimating item difficulty, not a measurement of this marker, and the harness makes no certification claim until a real gold set replaces its synthetic seed (`grade3-reading/ti-courseplans/courses/g4g5-writing/approval-package/sources/CALIBRATION-HARNESS-SPEC.md`, lines 122-123).

evidence.quote: | 95% Limits of Agreement | **[−11.4, +11.1] RIT** | Individual scores may differ by up to ±11 RIT |

Statistical basis: the Bland-Altman method [ACADEMIC] is the standard approach for comparing two measurement instruments that measure the same construct on the same scale [AERA-2014; Kolen-Brennan-2014].
The r=0.948 measures ranking accuracy, not absolute accuracy.

predicts the LLM is **systematically too generous, and a bigger model makes it worse** — **a 0.8 correlation with a +0.7-band offset is a broken scorer.** Report false-high (safety- critical: a weak response scored 2) separately from false-low
**Agreement report — the SIGNED gap, not just correlation.**

citations.ref: Statistical methods for assessing agreement between two methods of clinical measurement (The Lancet, 1986)
